_about: Acceptance rows for placement 26.11.19: today's panels model (layoutPanels with the kits' rooms) against the DockState, window A and window B numbers, every window width 280..1279 px, height 800. 22 arrangements of the panels pages, annotations, findings, plus the generic thumbs anchor states and the sheet, padding and stored-width states. A row with no kind is a REGRESSION row: the DockState and today agree and must keep agreeing. kind target: the DockState differs today and the row holds TODAY'S result (what the kits draw), the value the library should reach; its gap names the gap (see _gaps). kind option: the library's own option, not a kit rule. A row with intended true holds the DockState's own result where it differs from today on purpose (a ruling: C9 vertical give-way, C27 float clearance), a regression row for the DockState, not a target; the anchorRailOrder and anchorGiveWayOrder states are rulings where today wins (target rows; fields anchorRect {x,y,w,h} and railX {side: x} added), the anchorRiderOverAnchor, pressWhileNarrow and resizeMemoryAfterJump states rulings where the DockState wins (intended rows; riderRects, press and history added: a row after a press or a resize history carries the DockState's previous layout, so it is history-dependent); the heightSweep states have heights (the panels' drawn heights, px) and forms rail (a panel in its rail form, a column of them is 32 wide). Format as window-a.json / window-b.json. extends window-a.json#three / window-b.json#three is that file's states.three; fields beside it replace (edges, floats) or merge per id (items). handFold is ride (the kits' rule; window-a's own three says bar) unless a state says otherwise. items: closed = not open (keeps its place, takes no room), from 1 = folded by hand, kept = keeps open, thumbs = a fixed anchor edge item. floats rects are {x,y,w,h} in the window; the stage is the window (inset = pad). layout fields: columns / columnWidths (open columns per side, outer first, members top to bottom, width as drawn), rails (segments per side, outer first), rides (a bar riding over its side's first open column), forms (bar = folded in place), floats (rect; form bar when folded), contentWidth (the pages, exact), columnX (drawn x of the open columns, anchor states), sheetFallback. A state's known names its KNOWN_DIFFS entries; variants named window-b carry window B rows only where it differs.

_gaps.ride-for-stacks: a column of two or more panels, all folded by hand, beside an open column rides over it (a bar each, as wide as that column, taking no width); the DockState sends it to the rail
_gaps.float-clamp-region: today clamps a float to [0, W − 2·pad] × [0, H] in the body's px; the DockState clamps to [pad, W − pad] × [0, H]; INTENDED: the DockState wins
_gaps.float-bar-height: a folded float's bar: the window-A rows hold h 30 (the DockState's bar form); today's kits draw 32 (their layout bar); INTENDED: the DockState's
_gaps.float-shrink: today makes a float no wider than a stage narrower than it; the DockState shrinks it to fit the stage less the inset (down to the item's floatMin)
_gaps.float-clear-decision: today lets a float cover docked items and rail segments; the DockState moves it clear (host rule C27): INTENDED, not a gap and not a target; the kits adapt, and the rows marked with it hold TODAY's result for reference only
_gaps.sheet-signal: the narrow fallback (one panel over the pages) is not readable from layout.content, which stays above contentMin because rails are narrow: the library should say it
_gaps.inset-only-while-docked: window A draws its stage padding only while something is beside the pages; the DockState insets always (contentWidth here is what is drawn)
_gaps.anchor-outside-inset: a fixed edge outside the stage padding with no gutter after it
_gaps.anchor-shrink-fold: a fixed edge that shrinks toward its minimum and folds into the rail under give-way, as the oldest column
_gaps.anchor-change-sides: a pure change that moves a fixed edge to the other side
_gaps.rail-order: a compact rail beside the thumbnail rail is the OUTERMOST strip, at the window edge, and the thumbnails sit inside it (placement 7b: today wins)

_numbers.windowA: card 220..640, gap 12, padding 24 (12 each side), rail 32 (slot 44), bar 30, thumbs 72 (56..200)

three._about: Window A's start, all open: the left stack folds whole into the rail, then everything is in rails.

pair._about: Pages closed: it keeps its place and takes no room.

none._about: Nothing open: the layout's content is the stage less the padding (see padding-always for what is drawn).

separate._about: Three columns: they fold oldest first.

keptAnnotations._about: A kept panel's column folds last.

foldedInStack._about: Folded by hand in a stack: a bar in place (forms.annotations bar), as wide as the column.

foldedWholeStack._about: Every panel of the column folded by hand: the column goes to its side's rail.

foldedAlone._about: A one-panel column folded by hand rides over its side's first open column, at its width, taking none.

foldedAloneBar._about: handFold bar: the same panel goes to the rail instead of riding. Rows are the library's option, not today's kits (they ride: see foldedAlone).

foldedStackBesideColumn._about: Two panels, all folded by hand, in a column beside an open column: today every one rides over that column (a bar each, as wide as it, taking no width). Target rows; the DockState sends the stack to the rail.

floatingOverColumn._about: A float dropped over a column: today it covers the column (target for the clamp rows); the DockState moves it clear (host rule C27). Decide which the kits want.

floatingClosed._about: A closed float keeps its rect and takes no room.

sheet-not-in-the-layout._about: All open; the narrow fallback (one panel at a time over the pages). Pinned: window A below 576, window B below 520.

padding-always._about: GAP inset only while docked: window A draws its 12 px stage padding only while something is beside the pages (an open column or a rail). With nothing docked the pages are the whole window; contentWidth here is the width DRAWN (body less the slots, less the padding while padded).

stored-widths-are-slots._about: Host-side, no library gap: the old store holds a column width as a slot (card + gap). The state's DockEdge.size is the card as drawn, so the host takes the gap off a width read from an old store. Row: sizes 400 and 320 drawn.

anchor-outside-the-padding._about: Window A's thumbnail rail (generic id thumbs): a ring-0 edge that takes nothing, 72 wide (56..200). Today it sits OUTSIDE the stage padding (x 0) with no gap after it; columnX are the drawn x. GAP anchor outside the inset: a per-edge gutter/inset exemption.

anchor-never-gives-way._about: Same state. Today the thumbnail column is the OLDEST column: under give-way it shrinks toward 56 then folds into the left rail before the other columns. GAP shrink-fold under give-way for a fixed edge (the DockState's anchor never shrinks or folds).

anchor-keeps-its-side._about: Same state with the thumbnail rail moved to the RIGHT (Move to): today it is the outermost column of whichever side. GAP change sides: a pure change that moves a fixed edge to the other side.

heightSweepThree._about: INTENDED (C9 vertical give-way): a window 1120 wide, all open, from 900 down to 200 px high. Today shares the height equally at every height; the DockState folds the panel used longest ago to its header (forms bar) when the column is shorter than its panels' least heights (160 each, and the gaps), and a column of nothing but headers is its rail form (forms rail, the column 32 wide). Rows hold the DockState's result (heights = the panels' drawn heights), at the top and the bottom of each state.

heightSweepThreeInOne._about: INTENDED (C9): the three panels in ONE left column, 1120 wide, from 900 down to 200 px high: the oldest folds to its header first, then the next, then the whole column is its rail form. Today shares the height among the three at every height. Window B rows between 357 and 231 px are left out: there the stack steps the oldest panel to its RAIL form inside the open column, because that window's bar (38) is taller than the rail segment (36): a finding for placement, not a target. (Placement 7b: the bar 38 taller than the rail segment 36 is a library rule; the drawn heights are passed as they are, so there are no rows for it.)

anchorRailOrder._about: RULING (placement 7b): TODAY WINS. The thumbnail rail on the right (generic id thumbs), a column folded into the rail beside it: today's compact rail is the OUTERMOST strip, at the window edge, and the thumbnails sit inside it (railX.right > anchorRect.x); the DockState put the anchor outermost and the rail inside it. Rows are today's result, the target. Window A, rails left [pages, annotations] and right [findings] with the anchor open. rail-order applies to every row with an anchor and a rail beside it; a target and an intended row differ only by the host options (outsideInset: anchor at the window's edge, full height, no gutter, vs. inside the inset).

anchorRiderOverAnchor._about: RULING (placement 7b): THE STATE WINS. A panel folded by hand in a column of its own, with the thumbnail rail open: today rides it over the thumbnails (a 72 px bar at the window edge); the DockState rides it over the first open PANEL column, as wide as that column (riderRects), and, where none is open on its side, sends it to the side's rail. Rows are the DockState's result.

expect.note: no panel column is open on the anchor's side: the panel goes to the rail

anchorGiveWayOrder._about: RULING (placement 7b): TODAY WINS. The thumbnail rail is the oldest column: under give-way it shrinks first, 72 to 56 (from 1039 down; a card first shrinks at 1023, so the thumbs reach 56 at 1024), then folds into the left rail at 863, and the left stack follows at 851; with no anchor the stack folds at 807, and the DockState (the anchor never shrinks) folds it at 891. Bare arithmetic (no gap, no padding, rail 36): thumbs shrink from 991, a card from 975, the thumbs fold at 815, the stack at 795; the DockState 831, no anchor 759. Rows are today's result, the target.

expect.note: the sheet ignores the anchor (it folds into the rail like every column): one column 220 + 12 + contentMin 320 = 552 ≤ 566

pressWhileNarrow._about: INTENDED (C23, a press reshapes nothing): the window narrowed from 1400 to 700 px in steps of 10 (the left stack is folded into the rail by give-way), then a press on Pages. The DockState carries its previous layout: the layout after the press is the layout before it. Today re-ranks the columns by newest use and folds Findings instead. Rows are the DockState's result.

expect.note: room to spare: nothing changes in either model

resizeMemoryAfterJump._about: INTENDED (history under previous): three columns, pages and annotations on the left, findings on the right, the window jumped 1000 to 640 to 1000 px. The DockState carries its previous layout, so which column is the narrower after the jump depends on the history: it shrinks first the column it shrank before (here Findings, 288 and Annotations 300); today is stateless by age (Annotations 288, Findings 300). A resize a pixel at a time agrees in both. Rows are the DockState's result after the jump.

expect.note: history-dependent under previous: the same total width, the shrink on the other column than today
history-dependent under previous: Findings 268 and Annotations 280 where today has 280 and 268
